threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, roles and initial warehouse and office mapping tasks.

messages.text: Kicking off the warehouse move and office records consolidation for project_pack_ref: Warehouse Move & Office Records Consolidation. For this first phase we need to map the current warehouse layout and the office records. I can start sketching the aisles and zones into A1 and draft notes for T1. For office side, we need someone to own T3 and start filling A3. Proposal for scope to validate: warehouse zones Z1 to Z4 plus the small parts mezzanine, and office areas front office, finance room and archive room 1. Let us use this thread to confirm what is in scope and who owns updates to A1 and A3.

Thanks for starting this. On the office side, I can help with T3 and start listing filing cabinets and storage rooms into A3. Before I do that, can we clarify if archive room 2 is excluded for now and if digital-only folders are part of this first pass or only physical boxes and cabinets

Good question. From what I heard from the office administration manager, archive room 2 is lower priority and can wait until after the pilot. For now I suggest we include only physical records and supplies in T3 and just note where there are linked digital folders. We can extend A3 later with digital structure when we get to T9. Does that work for everyone

On the warehouse side, Z1 to Z4 plus mezzanine sounds fine to me. For T1 I can support by taking photos of current aisles and marking where we have high-turnover and dangerous goods. We should also capture current pain points like blocked aisles and where forklifts struggle to turn. Maybe we split zones so we do not overlap work.

I can walk Z3 and Z4 for T1 and note where we have heavy items and mixed pallets. I will need a bit of help with how to mark dangerous goods correctly in A1, so if someone can share a simple example or legend that would help.

For dangerous goods in A1, let us use a simple legend: red outline for dangerous pallets, yellow for fragile, and a note with the class where we know it. I will add a small key at the top of A1. For T1 split, I propose: I take Z1, Z2 and mezzanine, 153021 focuses on loading bays and staging, and 304178 covers Z3 and Z4 as suggested.

I can help with T3 as well, maybe by counting office supplies and listing them in A3. I am not fully sure how detailed the records inventory needs to be. Do we list every folder name or just box labels and date ranges

For T3, let us keep it practical: in A3 we list each cabinet, shelf and box with a short content type and date range, not every folder. For example: 'Finance cabinet 1, invoices, 2019 to 2020'. That should be enough for this phase and will help later when we digitise priority documents.

I can take the lead on listing all filing cabinets and storage rooms in A3, and 53954 can focus on office supplies stock. I will start with front office and finance room today, then move to archive room 1 tomorrow. I will also add a column in A3 for quick notes on confidentiality level so we can align later with T4.

Summing up scope so far: warehouse zones Z1 to Z4, mezzanine, loading bays and staging are in for T1. On office side, front office, finance room and archive room 1 are in for T3. Archive room 2 and purely digital folders will be handled in a later phase. Unless anyone objects by end of day, I will treat this as the agreed scope for this phase.

No objections from me. For ownership, I suggest 49303 is the main contact for updates to A1 and T1, since you are already defining the legend and zone split. For A3 and T3, maybe 112406 can be the main contact, with 53954 helping on supplies and counts.

I am ok with 112406 leading A3 and T3. I will focus on counting office supplies and tagging boxes with content type and date range as you both described. If I am unsure about a record type, I will leave a note in A3 for review.

Happy to be the main contact for A3 and T3. I will keep the sheet tidy and flag any questions about record categories or confidentiality so we can align with the office administration manager when we get to T4.

Then let us lock that in: I will own updates to A1 and progress on T1, and 112406 will own updates to A3 and progress on T3, with support from the rest of the team. I will also keep the warehouse supervisor in the loop on A1 changes so we can feed into T2 later.
Quick check: when we map Z3 and Z4 for T1, do we need to note exact pallet counts in A1 or just general zones and main issues I can do a rough count but it might slow us down.

For T1, focus on zones, aisle widths, and where we have congestion or dangerous goods. No need for exact pallet counts in A1 at this stage. We will get more precise counts later when we update A8 for T10.

To close this thread from my side: scope for this phase is confirmed as Z1 to Z4, mezzanine, loading bays and staging on the warehouse side, and front office, finance room and archive room 1 on the office side. Ownership is 49303 for A1 and T1, and 112406 for A3 and T3. I will brief the office administration manager so they know who to contact for updates.

threads.thread_goal: Define the move schedule and resource plan across shifts.

messages.text: We need to lock dates and time windows for moving the priority warehouse zones and office archives. I have started drafting A5 for T5 with proposed windows outside peak hours and a first pass at mover and clerk assignments. A6 will hold the box and pallet tracking log for T7. Let us use this thread to refine the schedule and confirm how many people we assign per batch.

Looking at A5 draft, the late evening slots for Z1 and Z2 work for forklifts, but the early morning slot for mezzanine might clash with inbound unloading. We should check with the warehouse supervisor before we freeze that. For T5 I suggest we keep moves to 2 hour blocks and leave at least 1 hour buffer before the first outbound wave.

For staffing, my view is that each warehouse batch needs at least 2 movers plus 1 forklift operator, especially when we touch dangerous goods. For the office archive batches, 1 mover and 1 clerk might be enough if we keep the volume small. We also need to factor in time for updating A6 during each batch for T7, otherwise the log will fall behind.

If we have 2 movers per batch, I would prefer one person focuses on moving and the other on stacking and updating A6. I can take the stacking and logging role for the first few batches while I get used to the tracking format in T7.

On the office side, I reviewed A5 and the proposed evening slots for archive room 1 look fine, but we should avoid end of month for finance room moves because of closing activities. For T5 I suggest we schedule finance room batches in the second week, midweek evenings, and keep front office moves to early evenings when call volume is lower.

I can help with T7 by entering box IDs into A6, but I might be slower at first. Could we plan slightly longer time windows for the first archive batch so we do not rush the logging Also, do we already know the exact format for the unique IDs or is that still open

For A6, I propose we use a simple format: WH for warehouse pallets and OF for office boxes, followed by zone or room and a running number, for example OF-AR1-001. I will document this in the header of A6 for T7. For the first archive batch we can book a 3 hour slot instead of 2 hours to give more time for logging.

I spoke briefly with the warehouse supervisor. They are ok with late evening moves for mezzanine but prefer we avoid early mornings due to inbound congestion. So for T5 in A5, let us move mezzanine batches to late evening on days without big inbound deliveries. I will mark suggested days and we can confirm once we see next weeks inbound plan.

For Z1 and Z2, I recommend we schedule them on separate days in A5 so we do not overload the team. Each of those zones has a lot of high-turnover items. If we try to do both in one evening, we risk running into outbound prep time.

The ID format for A6 works for me. For office batches in T5, I suggest we plan: front office on two evenings next week, finance room on two evenings in week two, and archive room 1 spread across three evenings. That should give us enough time to log everything properly in A6 without blocking day work.

I have updated A5 with separate evenings for Z1 and Z2, late evening slots for mezzanine on low inbound days, and the office pattern 112406 suggested. Each warehouse batch now shows 2 movers plus 1 forklift operator, and each office batch shows 1 mover plus 1 clerk, with a longer slot for the first archive batch to stabilise T7 logging.

From a warehouse operations view, the updated A5 looks workable. All moves are outside peak hours, and we have buffers before outbound prep. I would like one more confirmation from office side that the finance and front office slots do not clash with their deadlines, then we can treat this as our baseline schedule for T5.

I checked with the finance team informally. The week two evening slots in A5 should be fine as long as we avoid the last two days of the month. The front office slots also look ok since they are not during call peaks. I am comfortable with this schedule for T5.

Agreed, the office time windows in A5 work for us. We will make sure at least one clerk is available for each batch and that someone is explicitly responsible for updating A6 during the office moves for T7.

Based on confirmations from warehouse and office, we can approve the move schedule in A5 as the baseline for this phase of T5. I will note that any changes due to unexpected operational load will be handled in the twice-weekly schedule review, but the structure and staffing per batch stay as defined.

To be explicit on staffing: each warehouse batch will have 2 movers plus 1 forklift operator, and each office batch will have 1 mover plus 1 clerk, with 304178 focusing on stacking and logging in A6 for the first warehouse batches and 53954 supporting logging for the first archive batch in T7. If no one raises issues, we will treat this as the agreed staffing model.

No issues from me. The 2 movers plus 1 forklift operator setup is realistic for the loads we have, and having a dedicated person on A6 logging during the first runs will help us avoid missing IDs in T7.

Then we can record that staffing decision: 2 movers plus 1 forklift operator per warehouse batch, and 1 mover plus 1 clerk per office batch, as reflected in A5 and supported by the logging approach in A6 for T7.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in safety, stacking and confidentiality rules before the pilot move.

messages.text: Before we run the pilot move for one warehouse zone and one archive section under T8, we need to finalise the safety checklist and confidentiality rules. I have drafted A2 for T6 with lifting limits, stacking heights and dangerous goods notes, and 136230 has a first version of A4 for T4. Let us review both here so we can approve them ahead of the pilot.

I went through A2. The stacking height limits look reasonable, but for mixed pallets we might need a clearer rule. Right now it just says to keep heavy items at the bottom. Maybe we should add a maximum overhang and a reminder not to stack dangerous goods above head height.

In A2 I was not fully sure about the lifting limits section. It lists weights but not many examples. Could we add a simple table with common items we handle, like small cartons, medium boxes, and furniture pieces, so it is easier to apply during T6 training

Good points. I will update A2 to add: no overhang beyond 5 cm on any side, no dangerous goods stacked above shoulder height, and a note that mixed pallets must be wrapped after each layer. I will also add the examples 304178 suggested so the lifting limits are easier to understand during T6 briefings.

On the records side, A4 currently defines three categories: public, internal and confidential. For T4, access to confidential records is limited to named clerks and managers, and boxes must be sealed and labelled with category and date range, not detailed content. During the pilot under T8, only the assigned clerk should open boxes from archive room 1, and any digitisation should happen directly into the secure folders.

A4 looks clear overall. One question: for internal records that are not strictly confidential, can movers carry unsealed boxes between rooms during T8, or do we still want everything sealed I want to make sure we do not slow down the pilot more than needed.

I am ok with the three categories in A4, but I would appreciate a short checklist version for T4 that I can keep at my desk, with simple do and do not points. For example, when to lock cabinets, when to use covers on boxes, and how to handle shredding for non-needed copies.

For internal records during T8, I suggest we allow movers to carry unsealed boxes only within the same floor and only if the clerk is present and has logged the box in A6. For confidential records, boxes must be sealed and carried directly between designated points. I will add this nuance to A4 so it is clear.

I have now updated A2 with the extra examples and stacking rules. Once the health and safety officer reviews it, we can treat it as our reference for T6 and for the pilot under T8. For the pilot zone, I propose we enforce all A2 rules strictly so we can see if anything is unrealistic before we roll out wider.

I agree with using the full A2 rules in the pilot. That will show us if any of the stacking or lifting guidance is too strict for real operations. I do not see any blockers in the current version, as long as we remind everyone about the dangerous goods height rule before we start T8.
With the examples added, A2 is much clearer for me. I will need a quick run-through before the pilot as part of T6, but I do not have further changes to suggest.

I will add a one-page checklist version of A4 with do and do not points for T4, including when to lock cabinets, when to seal boxes, and how to handle shredding. For the pilot in T8, we will also require that any digitised confidential documents are stored only in the secure folders and that temporary files are deleted after upload.

With those additions, I am comfortable using A4 as our rule set for the pilot. I will make sure only the assigned clerk handles confidential boxes during T8 and that we follow the logging rules in A6.

Given the feedback and pending review by the health and safety officer, I propose we approve A2 as the safety checklist for lifting, stacking and dangerous goods for this project. If the officer suggests minor tweaks, we can incorporate them without changing the core rules before T8.
I support approving A2 as it stands, with the understanding that the health and safety officer can still refine wording. The operational guidance is solid enough for the pilot in T8.
Ok, we will record A2 as the approved safety checklist for lifting, stacking and dangerous goods for this project, subject to any minor wording updates from the health and safety officer.

On confidentiality, we now have A4 with categories, access rules, sealing rules and digitisation guidance, plus a short checklist version for daily use. For the pilot in T8, we will apply these rules strictly and adjust only if we find practical issues. Unless there are objections, we can treat A4 as the confirmed rule set for handling and digitising records during moves.
No objections from me. I will brief the other clerks on A4 and make sure they understand the difference between internal and confidential handling during T8.
Then we will record A4 as the confirmed confidentiality rule set for handling and digitising records during moves, including the pilot under T8.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot move results and adjust layout, schedule and logs.

messages.text: Pilot move for Z1 partial and archive room 1 section A under T8 is complete. No incidents or missing items reported, but we saw a few issues with pallet flow and logging in A6. Let us use this thread to capture lessons learned and decide what to change in A1, A5 and A6 before we scale up.

From the warehouse side, the main issue I saw was congestion near the temporary staging area. In A1 the current layout has that corner too close to the main aisle. For T2 I suggest we shift the staging zone one bay over and widen the turning space. Also, the loading sequence we followed did not fully match the plan in A1, which caused a small delay at the dock.

On logging, I missed updating A6 for two pallets during the busiest part of the move. We caught it later, but it shows that having one person both stacking and logging is risky. For T7 I think we should assign a dedicated logger for each batch, at least while we get used to the process.

From the archive side, A6 worked but we had a few moments where the mover was waiting for me to finish logging before they could take the next box. For T7 we might speed things up by pre-labelling boxes with IDs from A6 before the batch starts, then just ticking them off as they move.

I agree. When I helped with logging in A6, pre-written labels would have saved time. I also noticed that the A5 time window for the archive batch was just enough; if we had any extra questions about records, we might have run over. Maybe we should add a small buffer to the office batches in T5.

On schedule, the warehouse batch finished slightly early, but the archive batch used almost the full slot in A5. For T5 I suggest we keep warehouse windows as they are but extend archive room 1 batches by 30 minutes to allow for logging and any questions about record categories.

I support moving the temporary staging area in A1. During the pilot I had to stop the forklift twice to let people pass. For T2 we should also adjust the loading sequence so that pallets closest to the dock are loaded last, to avoid double handling.

I will update A1 to move the staging area one bay over and widen the turning space, and I will adjust the loading sequence in T2 so that we load from furthest to closest to the dock. That should reduce congestion and double handling in future batches.
If we assign a dedicated logger for T7, I am happy to take that role for the next few warehouse batches while someone else focuses on stacking. That way we can make sure A6 is always up to date.

I like the idea of pre-labelling. For T7 I can prepare a list of IDs in A6 before each archive batch and stick labels on boxes ahead of time. During the move we then just confirm movement and destination in A6 instead of writing IDs from scratch.

Given what we saw, I agree we should change the standard so that each batch has a dedicated logger for A6 under T7. For warehouse batches, that can be one of the movers; for office batches, one of the clerks. We will reflect this in A5 so staffing is clear.

I have updated A5 to mark a dedicated logger for each batch and extended archive room 1 time windows by 30 minutes. I also added a note in A6 instructions under T7 about pre-labelling IDs before each batch.

From my side, these changes cover the main issues we saw in the pilot: less congestion thanks to the new staging position in A1, clearer loading sequence in T2, and more robust logging in A6 with the dedicated logger and pre-labelling in T7.
I confirm that the extended archive time windows in A5 and the pre-labelling approach in A6 will work for the office team. We will adjust our prep so labels are ready before each batch under T7.

To summarise proposed changes after the pilot: update A1 to move the staging area and adjust turning space, update T2 loading sequence to load from furthest to closest to the dock, update A5 to include a dedicated logger and longer archive windows, and update A6 instructions under T7 to use pre-labelled IDs. If everyone agrees, we will adopt these changes for the remaining batches.
I agree with that summary. These adjustments keep us within constraints and should reduce the risk of congestion and logging gaps as we scale beyond the pilot.
No further changes from me. Let us lock in these updates so we can move on to the next zones with more confidence.
We will record that the layout plan in A1, the move schedule in A5, and the tracking log approach in A6 are now updated as described and will be used for all remaining batches after the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Close out the project with final SOP, training recap and next steps.

messages.text: We are at the point where main moves are done and inventories updated, so we can close out project_pack_ref: Warehouse Move & Office Records Consolidation. A7 now holds the draft move SOP and lessons learned for T11, and A8 has the updated equipment and furniture inventory from T10. Let us review the SOP, confirm training coverage from T12, and agree how we will maintain the SOP going forward.

I reviewed the warehouse sections of A7. The layout and loading steps match what we are actually doing now, including the updated staging area and loading sequence from T2. The safety section references A2 and T6 correctly. One thing we might add is a short checklist for pre-move equipment checks, based on what we saw during T12 briefings.

On training, we held short briefings for each shift as part of T12. Attendance is noted in A7, and we captured common questions about stacking and logging. I think the SOP should highlight that any new hires must go through the same briefing before they work in the new layout.

I checked A8 and the equipment list looks complete to me. We recorded the new locations for forklifts, pallet jacks and main racks, and noted one damaged trolley. I do not see any gaps, but if someone spots missing items we can still add them.

On the office side, A7 includes the records consolidation steps and references A3, A4 and A6. For T11 I would like to add a short section on how we digitised priority documents under T9, including naming conventions and where to store the index so staff can find files quickly.

I agree. During T9 I sometimes had to ask where to save scanned files and how to name them. If A7 includes a simple example, like folder path and file name pattern, it will help others avoid the same questions.

I will add a section to A7 describing the digital filing structure from T9, with a clear example of folder paths and file names, and a note that the index is stored in the shared drive. That should make it easier for staff to follow the same pattern.

I have added a pre-move equipment checklist to A7, covering forklift checks, pallet jack condition and availability of straps and wrap, based on what we used during T12. With that, I think the warehouse part of the SOP is ready.
I just re-read the updated A7. The flow from planning, through A5 and A6, to execution and training is clear. I do not have further changes to suggest.
With the digital filing section added, the office part of A7 looks good to me. It reflects how we handled confidentiality with A4 and how we used A3 and A6 during the move.
I am comfortable using A7 as our reference going forward. The examples make it easier to follow, especially for scanning and naming files from T9.

On training, T12 is complete for all current staff, and A7 records attendance and key questions. For future moves, I suggest we keep a simple rule: anyone new to the warehouse or office must read A7 and attend a short briefing before they participate in moves.
That rule works for me. It will keep everyone aligned with the layout in A1, the schedule approach in A5 and the logging rules in A6 without having to rediscover lessons from this project.
We should also decide who will keep A7 up to date. My suggestion is that 136230 owns the document overall, with 49303 and me proposing updates when layouts or record processes change.

I can take ownership of A7 in the shared drive. When warehouse or office processes change, 49303 and 112406 can send me notes, and I will update the SOP and log the change date. That way we keep a single source of truth for future moves.
From my side, A7 now reflects how we actually work, and we have a clear owner and update process. I am ok to sign off this SOP as the reference for future warehouse and office moves.
I agree with signing off A7. It captures the key steps and checks we need, and the training rule from T12 will keep new people aligned.
No objections from office side. A7 and A8 give us a good baseline for future audits and moves.
We will record that A7 is the final move SOP for this project, stored in the shared drive, with 136230 as owner and 49303 and 112406 as main contributors for future updates.
